payload.native_system_prompt:
You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

### Glossary of tags that will be sent to you:
# - <LM_SYSTEM_PROMPT>: The system prompt for the language model.
# - <LM_INPUT>: The input to the language model.
# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Move the mug to the right of the headphones
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Comparing the source and edited images, is the source mug's move to the right of the headphones complete, visibly in progress but incomplete, or not visibly made?
node.criteria: Pass only when visual correspondence supports that the source mug itself is positioned to the right of the headphones in the edited image. Fail when the source mug is identifiable and either remains at its source-side position without discernible movement toward the right, or has visibly moved toward the right but remains short of the requested position; the latter is incomplete progress, not completion. Do not infer no progress merely because the source mug is not established as the right-side mug, completion is unproven, or a mug remains left of the headphones. Compare source-specific features and spatial changes across all plausible edited objects and remnants: altered color, size, or appearance alone does not rule out identity, and a right-side mug alone does not establish identity or completion. Use unknown if the source mug's correspondence or whether it moved cannot be determined from the visual evidence.
node.binding: Compare the source light-blue mug, including its body shape, handle, scale, appearance, and original position left of the headphones, with all mug-like objects and remnants in the edited image. Assess the pale mug left of the headphones, the mug right of them, and the blue-looking blurred patch at far left as possible correspondence evidence. Neither the patch nor either mug conclusively establishes identity or lack of movement. Determine whether source-specific visual evidence supports completion to the right of the headphones, visible movement toward the right that remains incomplete, or no discernible movement. Do not use mug count or right-side position alone; retain unknown if correspondence or movement remains genuinely indeterminate.

node_traces.evidence: The source light-blue mug is clearly left of the headphones. In the edited image, there is a blue blurred patch at far left, a pale mug left of the headphones, and a mug to their right. The edited mugs differ in appearance from the source, and the blurred patch does not establish that the source mug moved from its original position. The visual evidence does not reliably identify which edited object, if any, corresponds to the source mug or establish its movement.

response.content: {"text":"The binding already names the plausible objects and correctly preserves unknown, but it may over-anchor the evaluator on identity uncertainty: the edited image shows the original blue mug-shaped appearance as a blurred patch at far left, while a pale mug is left of the headphones and another mug is right of them. Refine the decision procedure to assess partial progress independently from proving that the right-side mug is the source mug: compare the source mug’s location and distinctive shape/handle against every candidate and remnant, and ask whether any evidence supports movement toward the right even if correspondence is uncertain. Do not treat the blurred patch as proof of no movement, or the right-side mug as proof of completion; likewise, appearance changes alone do not disqualify identity. The trace is valid uncertainty, not a transport, schema, or dependency failure, so avoid forcing the reference label. Its high confidence despite unresolved correspondence is a calibration signal: distinguish confidence in observed layout from confidence in identity and movement, and retain unknown only when the evidence cannot resolve those questions."}
